Javanese Weton: Your Day and Market Day

Javanese tradition gives every day two names: one from the seven-day week and one from the five-day market week (pasaran). The pair on your birthday is your weton, and each name carries a value called neptu. Enter your birth date to see yours, watch how it is counted, then explore all 35.

    About this tradition

    What is a weton?

    The Javanese calendar runs two weeks side by side: the seven-day week used around the world, and an older five-day week of market days, Legi, Pahing, Pon, Wage and Kliwon, once tied to markets that moved from town to town. Together they make 35 different pairs, and the same pair returns every 35 days. Javanese calendars still print both.

    Primbon books, such as the Kitab Primbon Betaljemur Adammakna, give each day and each market day a number (neptu) and add them. Tradition uses the totals when comparing two birthdays or choosing a day for an event. Fate Tutor shows the numbers and how they are added, and does not judge any total as better or worse.

    In Javanese reckoning a new day begins at sunset, not at midnight. Sunset in Java is close to 18:00 all year, so Fate Tutor treats a birth at or after 18:00 on the clock as an evening birth and shows both wetons: the one of the calendar date and the next day's. Families differ on which they use; ask yours.

    These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
